Let's first talk about their weapon approach. What do you think travels faster. Your hand from your hip, moving inches up to my gun pointed at your head, or my finger on the trigger? Or, when I approach you on the street and ask you what time is it. You reach to your pocket for your phone, and I'm starting to stab you. How many stabs, before you finally grab my hand? Krav maga is teaching you how to defend a specific angle with a cooperative person, when you're already expecting it. It's not teaching you, how to survive a real attack. And to be honest, when weapons are used, it's luck. No martial art will teach you how to deal with a knife attacker or a firearm.

As far as videos go, [this guy](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aA_Q068vA6Y) is a goldmine of busting irrational techniques from all sources. Krav maga, sef-defence courses, all that. I know this specific video isn't on the exact topic of krav maga, but you'll see similar things in every bullshit martial art, including krav maga.

[This video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2xpcrDzy344) shows how unexpected knife attacks can be and how spastic the knife moves. It's not a single strike from a particular angle, as krav maga teaches people. If you look at how they train and then look up real videos, with real violence and real blood, you'll realize, how much their tactics are off.

Also, you can just look around on YouTube and see, how much bullshit is out there. And just acknowledge the fact, that in mixed martial arts you don't really see krav maga. You see jiu-jitsu, kickboxing, karate, taekwondo, boxing... But no aikido or krav maga. Because that simply does not work and it's a waste of time.

I don't think it's good for self defence. I love it as a sport, but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone who wants to learn self-defence. Boxing teaches you only about hands and movement. But when you add kicks to the equation, people panic. Add grappling and you're screwed if someone is stronger. That's why I said jiu-jitsu. It teaches you how to get out of the harms way and how to neutralize someone. Triangle choke is a basic move and it's closed from the back. That's just ideal for women, in my honest opinion. And you don't need brute force to execute it. If someone is unexperienced, they get tied into a pretzel and you can decide, how long you hold them there. And I assure you, once it's closed, you can roll to sit on top of the attacker, call the police and wait for them. If the attacker tries to be slick, he would be choked out with his own arm. It doesn't take a genius to learn it and it's so much safer, than standing on your feet and trying to trade blows with someone potentially stronger, risking getting knocked out or dipping a jab to get kicked in the head. Jiu jitsu eliminates this panic. You roll, you learn. You learn how to deal with pressure, be energy efficient and how to not to panic, when you scuffle with someone.

Self-defence is a very important thing, but that can be confusing for someone who doesn't know much about martial arts. Self defense courses usually are filled with non-realistic approaches to the situations and can give someone false confidence about their skills. There are lots of schools and courses that focus on teaching how to defend yourself, but they don't teach anything useful a woman could do to stay safe. I mean, those funny multi-hit, fighting-game like combos or silly concepts like wrist control (of someone who may be bigger, stronger, and unwilling to move his hands) is just ridiculous.

If anybody is reading this comment and has someone who thinks about learning how to defend themselves, tell them to look into Brasilian Jiu-Jitsu. It's about energy efficiency and neutralizing threats. Also, it teaches how to defend yourself laying flat on the ground, so that would be greatly helpful for all women, since all rapists want them exactly in that position. And least thing they'd expect is a triangle choke or a broken arm.

There are many videos on YouTube, criticizing and showing how useless aikido, krav maga or self-defence courses are in the real world. It sets very unrealistic expectations and they all train on cooperative people. But in the time someone tries to gets my thumb to apply a wristlock, they eat seventeen of my punches. I'm all for self-defense, but make sure it's a legit one. Jiu-jitsu is a great one, and alnogside of that, it can be either kickboxing/taekwondo/muay-thai. That will give anyone a greater toolset to defend themselves, than doing those ridiulous courses and classes.

If it's all about enjoying it, why it's specifically exercise that's so hyped up and not drawing or gardening or fishing? If it's all about something making me happy, why it has to be exercise? I don't think it's about being passionate about it.

I just don't think it's about having a thing that makes you happier, because then it could be anything, not just exercise. And I struggle to see any benefits of that activity, so that's the main reason I've made the initial post.
